lecture: فلسفه‌ی سیاسی با تکیه بر لیبرالیسم (جلسه ششم بخش اول؛ جلسه سوم بخش دوم؛ جلسه پنجم بخش دوم)
lecture_source: Sabouri, D. (n.d.). فلسفهٔ سیاسی با تکیه بر لیبرالیسم، جلسهٔ ششم (بخش اول) [ویدیو]. YouTube, کانال @darwinsabouri. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AClcVqTJNyw ؛ جلسهٔ سوم (بخش دوم): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DOi52jMYY8c ؛ جلسهٔ پنجم (بخش دوم): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RCqiDFmoqo4
speaker: Sabouri, D.
summary_of_lecture_fa: این فایل سه بخش از یک دورهٔ فلسفهٔ سیاسی با محور لیبرالیسم است. بخش اول لیبرالیسم را یک چالش اخلاقی می‌خواند که مرجعیت سنتی را کنار می‌زند و فرد را در مرکز می‌گذارد. بخش دوم کلاس‌گفتگو دربارهٔ هابز و ماکیاولی و جدایی اخلاق از سیاست است. بخش سوم به مونتسکیو می‌پردازد: قانون، آزادی و تفکیک قوا. سخنران نگاهی همدلانه به سنت لیبرال دارد و بخش‌هایی از آن را رأی شخصی خودش اعلام می‌کند.

quality_notes: The file holds three class recordings (session 6 part 1, session 3 part 2, session 5 part 2) with heavy ASR noise, many side conversations with students, and some passages that are only partly intelligible. Names and book titles are garbled in places (for example Sophocles, Mises and Hayek references); I used them only where context was certain. Part 1 is a monologue with the lecturer's own strong thesis; part 2 is Hobbes discussed through readings from Leviathan and student questions; part 3 is Montesquieu with long quoted passages from a Persian translation of The Spirit of the Laws. I left out remarks on current Iranian politics and the comparison of Montesquieu's chambers with Iranian institutions, side anecdotes (films, football, apartment living, Stanford and Milgram experiments raised by a student), and the claim about the date of the first Persian translation (numbers garbled). Sophocles, 'Lenin brick' and Abazari video references could not be verified and were not used. Whether Spirit of the Laws first appeared in Geneva rather than the Netherlands was not asserted. Point-level claims on Good Samaritan and duty-to-rescue laws are stated at a general level and should be checked for specific jurisdictions before use. The lecturer's reading of Montesquieu's slavery passages as explanation rather than endorsement is reported as his view.
